name: Enoxaparin
route_note: subcutaneous injection once or twice daily from prefilled syringes; IV bolus in some ACS protocols

discovery.note: Produced by alkaline depolymerisation of benzyl esters of porcine heparin.

tagline: Low-molecular-weight heparin that made outpatient clot treatment routine
summary: Enoxaparin is a low-molecular-weight heparin made by chemically breaking down porcine heparin. Its shorter chains act mainly on factor Xa via antithrombin, giving predictable weight-based dosing by subcutaneous injection without routine monitoring.
mechanism: Like heparin, enoxaparin binds antithrombin through a pentasaccharide sequence. Most of its chains are too short to bridge antithrombin to thrombin, so it inhibits factor Xa more than thrombin (anti-Xa:anti-IIa ratio about 4:1).
Lower binding to plasma proteins and cells gives more predictable absorption and a longer half-life than unfractionated heparin. Protamine only partially reverses its effect.
uses: Prophylaxis of deep vein thrombosis in surgical and medical patients
Treatment of DVT with or without pulmonary embolism

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Lovenox for DVT prophylaxis after hip replacement.

history.title: Neuraxial warning
history.detail: The FDA warns of spinal/epidural haematomas with LMWHs and neuraxial anaesthesia, later made a boxed warning.

history.title: ExTRACT-TIMI 25
history.detail: In STEMI treated with fibrinolysis, enoxaparin reduces death or recurrent infarction at 30 days compared with unfractionated heparin, at the cost of more major bleeding.

history.title: US generic
history.detail: The FDA approves the first generic enoxaparin (Sandoz), after a debate over how to show sameness of a complex mixture.

history.title: EU biosimilars
history.detail: Biosimilar enoxaparin products are authorised in the EU.

pk.excretion: Renal; dose reduction needed in severe renal impairment

safety.boxed_warning: Epidural or spinal haematomas, possibly causing permanent paralysis, can occur with neuraxial anaesthesia or spinal puncture.

facts: It is the most widely used low-molecular-weight heparin worldwide.
It is commonly preferred to warfarin for anticoagulation during pregnancy because it does not cross the placenta.
